projects.name: USAID Partnering for Resilience Program
projects.description:
The USAID-funded Partnering for Resilience Program is implemented by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in partnership with four UN Agencies: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) and United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN Women). The project aims to foster the peacebuilding and conflict transformation with an ultimate goal to promote an enabling environment for sustainable peace. The project builds on the success and lessons learned from previous and current interventions of UNDP and UN partner organizations in support of conflict-affected communities and the lasting peace in general. The project expects to achieve the following results: 
1.1: Increased public support for conflict transformation and lasting peace (UNDP, UNICEF, UN Women)
1.2: Improved capacity of youth in business education and increased demand for production and trade (FAO, 
1.3: Enhanced community resilience by improved access to diverse sources of social services (UNDP, UNFPA, UNICEF)

2.1: Increased exposure for changemakers to international and/or unique opportunities (FAO, UNICEF)
2.2: Sustained professional networks and partnerships across dividing lines (UNDP, UNICEF, UNFPA)

3.1: Robust contextual information generated (FAO, UNDP, UNFPA, UNICEF, UN Women, WHO)
3.2: Complexity-aware monitoring of programmatic implementation established (UNDP).
projects.outcome: 4.2 Improved socio-economic conditions, resilience and self-reliance in conflict-affected communities

projects.description:
Joint initiative of the EU and the United Nations (UN) implemented as a joint programme (JP) by the UNDP and OHCHR aiming at ensuring  better protection of human rights for all in Georgia, including those in vulnerable situation - complies with the international obligations of Georgia, deriving from UN human rights treaties, EU-Georgia Association Agreement (AA), as well as other documents forging Georgia’s path to EU integration including nine steps outlined by the European Commission, Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) as well as with the national priorities..

OUTCOME: AN ENABLING ENVIRONMENT CREATED FOR GREATER GENDER EQUALITY AND WOMEN’S EMPOWERMENT (GEWE)

projects.name: USAID Partnering for Resilience Program
projects.description:
The USAID-funded Partnering for Resilience Program is implemented by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in partnership with four UN Agencies: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) and United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN Women). The project aims to foster the peacebuilding and conflict transformation with an ultimate goal to promote an enabling environment for sustainable peace. The project builds on the success and lessons learned from previous and current interventions of UNDP and UN partner organizations in support of conflict-affected communities and the lasting peace in general. The project expects to achieve the following results: 
1.1: Increased public support for conflict transformation and lasting peace (UNDP, UNICEF, UN Women)
1.2: Improved capacity of youth in business education and increased demand for production and trade (FAO, 
1.3: Enhanced community resilience by improved access to diverse sources of social services (UNDP, UNFPA, UNICEF)

2.1: Increased exposure for changemakers to international and/or unique opportunities (FAO, UNICEF)
2.2: Sustained professional networks and partnerships across dividing lines (UNDP, UNICEF, UNFPA)

3.1: Robust contextual information generated (FAO, UNDP, UNFPA, UNICEF, UN Women, WHO)
3.2: Complexity-aware monitoring of programmatic implementation established (UNDP).

●	Improved knowledge of local stakeholders and their active engagement in SDG localization.
●	Inclusive national and local governance systems have greater resilience and capacities to ensure evidence-based and participatory policymaking, adopt, implement and monitor SDGs and deliver quality services to all.
●	Advanced innovative public services and digital inclusion practices.

In 2025: 2 further in-person sessions of the Coordination Committee on the Trans-Caspian and Almaty-Tehran-Istanbul Corridors which is convening periodically as a group of friends of the Chair of the Working Party on Transport Trends and Economics (WP.5). Location of the meetings yet to be determined. The Coordination Committee convenes on the basis of an agreed 2023-2025 biennial programme of work based on 5 thematic clusters: 1. transport infrastructure harmonization; 2. transport documents and digitalization; 3. harmonization of tariffs and time schedules; 4. border crossing efficiency and 5. economic viability, climate change resilience and environmental performance. Typically, every country is represented at every meeting by 2-3 representatives from either the Ministry of transport and/ or railway and customs authorities.

projects.description:
To strengthen the sustainable management of forests and enhance the contribution of forests and forest products to sustainable development in the ECE region:UNDA project “Circular forest product value chains and nature-based solutions in Central Asia and the Caucasus” is aimed at improving knowledge and capacity to advance inclusive and resilient post-pandemic rural development and forest landscape restoration through circular forest product value chains and nature-based solutions.
Planned activities for 2024:
1. Conduct a national market gap assessment of circular value chains for non-wood forest products including assessments of the economic, social and environmental value of forest landscapes.
2. Organize a national workshop on circular value chains for forest products based on the national market assessments, for validation, dissemination and capacity building.
